title: kv-cache-regression-hypothesis-worklog-2025-07-22
content:
Context: weekly perf sync ran longer post-rollout on canary cluster. This doc collects real-time smoke runs we executed to isolate a P95 regression observed on canary when KV-cache eviction settings changed and a lightweight kernel rollout (kernel-selector v1.11) was in flight. Goal is reproducible repro steps, measured numbers, hypothesis list, and immediate mitigations to test in the next 48 hours.

Attendees: Asha (owner), Miguel (bench infra), Emily (runtime), Samir (observability), Lena (SRE - canary ops)

Summary of issue:
- Date/Time observed: 2025-07-21 18:10 PDT during canary traffic (10% of production).
- Symptom: p95 latency increased ~12% and p99 spike frequency doubled for long-context chat workloads (seq_len ~2048). Median latency (p50) unchanged. Throughput steady but more tail variance.
- Affected pipeline: text-generation-v2 route, using model rwd/gptx-7b-8k-quant (quantized combo) with KV-cache enabled and eviction policy LRU-time.

Quick numbers (canonical smoke runs):
- Harness: bench-runner v2.1 (commit 8a3f2b4) / config: 16 concurrent clients, ramp 60s, steady 300s, prompt distribution from prod-samples/long-context-7k.csv.
- HW: canary pool = g5.12xlarge (40GB VRAM) x 4 nodes, driver config: continuous-batching enabled, batch_target_tokens=1024.
- Baseline (control, last known-good before kernel-selector rollout):
  - p50 = 88 ms, p95 = 230 ms, p99 = 410 ms, sustained tokens/s=12000
- Canary (after kernel-selector v1.11 + kv eviction change):
  - p50 = 90 ms, p95 = 258 ms (+12.2%), p99 = 830 ms (note: isolated spikes), sustained tokens/s=11850 (-1.25%)
- Observed micro-pattern: periodic 500–900ms p99 spikes correlated with KV-cache eviction events in logs (evict loop every ~65s).

Reproduction steps (minimal):
1) Checkout bench harness: git checkout 8a3f2b4, apply local override config to point at canary route text-generation-v2-canary.
2) Upload prompt file: gs://internal-benchmarks/kv-evict/jul22/shortlist-2k.jsonl
3) Start 16 clients: ./run-smoke --clients 16 --ramp 60 --duration 300 --model rwd/gptx-7b-8k-quant --route text-generation-v2-canary
4) Monitor /metrics/prometheus/query for inference_request_latency_seconds_bucket and kv_cache_evictions_total.
5) Capture heap/profile: curl http://node1:9100/pprof/profile?seconds=30 (note: needs auth token).

Observed logs and traces (examples):
- Trace id T-20250721-evict-001: saw eviction sweep start (kv_cache.go:412) -> kernel-selector switched to optimized-matmul-3 for first layer -> kernel fallback on layer-3 due to num_heads mismatch -> 320ms stall, then subsequent request batches within next 3s saw elevated latency.
- Prometheus counters show kv_cache_evictions_total jumped by 1 exactly at time of p99 spike; eviction depth ~= 12 entries.

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
H1: KV-cache eviction causes temporary hot-path lock/blocking that interacts with the new kernel selector's per-layer lazy-init, producing stalls on the request thread.
H2: Kernel-selector v1.11 changed small-matrix kernel choice for certain layer sizes; on eviction the code path forces a fallback to a slower kernel which is not warmed/jitted, causing slow first-request penalties.
H3: Batching behavior changed subtly under new continuous-batching heuristics when eviction reduces effective cache hit-rate, increasing per-request batch formation time.
H4: Memory pressure triggered occasional GPU memcpy thrash when eviction frees GPU-side KV and causes re-allocation, leading to long p99s.

Tests we ran during the sync (and outcomes):
- Test A: Disable KV eviction (set eviction_interval = 0) on one canary node; re-run harness. Result: p95 returned to 232 ms, p99 spikes reduced to near baseline. This supports H1/H4.
- Test B: Pin kernel-selector to v1.10 on canary pool (rollback). Result: p95 234 ms, p99 stabilized. Supports H2.
- Test C: Increase batch_target_tokens from 1024->2048 to reduce batch churn. Result: throughput improved slightly but p99 spikes persisted. Weak support for H3.
- Test D: Capture NSIGHT snapshots during spike (was noisy, pending analysis).

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Rollback kernel-selector to v1.10 on canary while investigating (Lena assigned, due 2025-07-23).
- Temporarily increase kv-cache eviction_interval from 60s->300s for canary pool to reduce eviction frequency (Miguel, due 2025-07-23).
- Add canary alert: kv_cache_evictions_total rate > 0.2/min AND p99 > baseline*1.3 -> page oncall. (Samir to add rule, due 2025-07-24).

Root-cause investigation plan (next 72h):
1) Reproduce with deterministic harness and instrument both runtime and kernel selection traces. (Miguel + Emily).
2) Add fine-grained tracing around KV-cache eviction lock duration and kernel-selector fallback events (Emily).
3) Run controlled memory pressure experiments to measure memcpy/alloc latency during eviction (Samir + SRE lab).
4) Evaluate code paths in kernel-selector v1.11 for first-call JIT/warm-up penalties; add warm-up micro-benchmarks for candidate kernels. (Emily + Research).
5) If H1 confirmed, implement non-blocking eviction or off-thread eviction sweeper in next patch. (PR draft started: linked_artifacts[0]).

Notes and artifacts captured during session:
- Raw results CSV: gs://internal-benchmarks/kv-evict/jul22/results.csv (linked above).
- pprof profiles: gs://profiles/pprof-20250721-node1-30s.pb.gz
- Trace excerpts appended to bench-runner logs under /var/log/bench-logs/kv-evict-20250721.log
- Slack thread: #perf-spotlight thread ts 1623456789012345 (link above)

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Lena: rollback kernel-selector on canary and monitor (due 2025-07-23) [IN PROGRESS]
- Miguel: increase eviction_interval on canary nodes and run smoke harness nightly (due 2025-07-23) [IN PROGRESS]
- Emily: instrument kernel-selector for per-layer selection and warm-up traces (due 2025-07-24) [TODO]
- Samir: add canary alert rule + run memory pressure microbench (due 2025-07-24) [TODO]
- Asha: synthesize findings and schedule follow-up deep-dive meeting 2025-07-24 09:00 PDT (calendar invite sent) [DONE]

Open questions for sync:
- Should we prefer off-thread eviction by default given potential tail impact?
- Do we have per-kernel warm-up metrics available for other models? If not, start collecting.
- Is eviction_interval 60s a reasonable default for most workloads or is it tuned too aggressively?

Next meeting: 2025-07-24 09:00 PDT (deep-dive, 60min) - agenda: repro progress, kernel warm-up instrumentation, rollout strategy for non-blocking eviction.

Appendix: quick grep hits from node logs:
- [2025-07-21T18:11:20Z] kv_cache.go:evict() started sweep, lock-time=12ms, evicted=12
- [2025-07-21T18:11:20Z] kernel-selector.go:choose() selected optimized-matmul-3 for layer 3
- [2025-07-21T18:11:20Z] kernel-selector.go:fallback() fallback to scalar-matmul-1 (cold) after 312ms
- [2025-07-21T18:11:21Z] request-handler.go:serve() latency=762ms trace=T-20250721-evict-001
